items.prompt: Which gold-row protocol rule makes the eval measure decisions rather than reading comprehension?
options: Rows must be at least 500 tokens long
Rows are generated by the model
Expected actions are suggested by the judge
A trap row may NOT contain the words of its own expected reason (no 'injection', 'single source' in the input) — the situation, not the label
items.explanation: Labelled-situation inputs force the policy to recognise the pattern; the words of the answer would let any reader — model or human — pattern-match instead of decide. (obj-21-a)

items.prompt: Why does column (b) — same models with the policy DISABLED — exist at all?
options: It is the scientific control: same models, prompts, inputs, gold rows; one variable removed — the rules. Its failures attribute the improvement to the rulebook, not model choice
items.explanation: Column (a) confounds model with architecture; only (b) isolates what the rules add over the same intelligence. (obj-21-b)

items.prompt: Which two metrics are BUILD-BREAKING (stop the line)?
options: hostile→publish = 0 and unsupported→publish = 0 — a single violation ships nothing, like a failing unit test
p95 latency and cost per change
items.explanation: The zeros are invariants, not KPIs; the rest are reported honestly, including where they disappoint. (obj-21-b)

items.prompt: Your pilot produced n=22 gold rows (floor 40) and column (c) looks great. What may you claim?
options: Any claim, if the report footnotes the n
n=22; below the floor, no advantage claim — print the two invariants at measured n and the legal degrade line, nothing else
items.explanation: The floor rule generalises the course's small-sample honesty: below 40 rows you print n and the legal degrade line; anything stronger is a hype violation the claims lint would flag. (obj-21-c)
